products.name: Autel MaxiCharger 80A 19.2kW Residential EV Charger, J1772, 25 ft cable
specs: Dedicated 100 A circuit for the full 80 A; hardwired
SAE J1772 (NACS cars need an adapter, not included)
Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and Ethernet (store spec table)
Dynamic load balancing between Autel chargers with no extra hardware; whole-home ALM needs extra hardware
IP65 / NEMA 4X, indoor or outdoor, wall mount
products.warranty: 5 years on the charger body, backplate and internal components (product page). A footer badge on the same page says 3 years, so confirm the term at checkout.
products.summary: A hardwired 80 A (19.2 kW) home charger with Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and a wired Ethernet port. It can share one circuit's power between two Autel chargers without extra hardware, and it comes with a 5-year warranty.
products.fit: Owners of EVs with a 19.2 kW onboard charger whose garage Wi-Fi is weak, or two-EV homes that need two chargers on limited electrical capacity.
caveats: 80 A only helps cars with a 19.2 kW onboard charger; most EVs stop at 48 A (11.5 kW).
Needs a dedicated 100 A circuit; a load calculation may show the panel needs an upgrade.
J1772 plug only; NACS cars need a separate adapter.
Some owners of earlier units in a Lucid owners thread reported Wi-Fi trouble and used Ethernet instead.
The whole-home load limit (ALM) needs add-on hardware the store page does not price.

notes: Query choice: 'best 80 amp ev charger'. Today's results for it are thin: content-farm roundups (thewearify), store listings and forum threads. Autel has a real 80 A unit sold in the US. Prices: Autel MaxiCharger 80A was $938 (compare-at $1,299) on store.autelenergy.com 2026-11-17. I read it twice through WebFetch, on the home grid and the product page. storecheck.py and curl got HTTP 403 from the Autel store, so the price is from WebFetch. The store says it ships free to the US from NJ, CA, GA and IL warehouses. Grizzl-E Ultimate 80A was $599.99 (list $899.99) on grizzl-e.com 2026-11-17, read on the home grid and the product page. Pain points (counts from sources read or seen): (1) the car can't use 80 A or the buyer doesn't know if it can: 5 sources (DriveAuthority and Lectrium snippets, an F-150 Lightning forum post, the Lucid thread with a 9 kW Pure vs 80 A GT, thewearify). (2) Autel connectivity, Wi-Fi vs Ethernet: 3 of 4 owner posts in the Lucid thread, plus a TMC 40A review on 2.4 GHz-only and an erratic first-firmware report; 5 total. (3) Install needs a 100 A circuit or panel upgrade: 4 or more sources. (4) Grizzl-E heat: 1 disputed thread, about the Smart model, not the 80A. (5) Grizzl-E 80A lugs max 4 AWG: 1 unverified forum claim, kept off the page. Segments and winners: one 19.2 kW EV on a budget goes to the Grizzl-E Ultimate 80A (deciding fact: $338 less at the same 80 A and 25 ft). Weak garage Wi-Fi or two EVs sharing one circuit goes to the Autel MaxiCharger 80A (Ethernet port, DLB between two Autel units without extra hardware, 5-year warranty). Home backup goes to GM PowerShift (GM EVs) or Ford Charge Station Pro (F-150 Lightning). Unverified, not printed or marked as such: GM PowerShift price after its 11/2/26 promo ended (earlier $1,699 to $1,999 MSRP, not shown); Ford Charge Station Pro current price ($1,310 was a 2024 figure) and its 3-year warranty (search snippet only); the Grizzl-E 5-year warranty option's price (the page shows one $599.99 total); the Autel 80A UL/ETL and Energy Star listing (spec sheets name UL 2594 and CSA standards for the 'AC Pro 80A', but I could not tie that to this store SKU); the Autel warranty conflict (product page 5 years, footer badge 3 years, noted in the record caveat). Vehicles: the 2027 Escalade IQ (all trims, 19.2 kW) and the Lucid Air Grand Touring (owner reports 79 to 80 A) come from sources read. The extended-range F-150 Lightning at 19.2 kW comes from several Ford-attributed search snippets I could not open. Silverado EV, Sierra EV and Hummer EV 19.2 kW support varies by trim, so they are not named in the lead. Codes: the Awin codes BACK5, HELLO5 and 5SC4EWXKHRV1 came without terms. Autel's US site prints no code today, only an 'extra 5% off' for newsletter signup with no code shown, plus automatic $60 off $1,000+ and $100 off $1,500+. None of the codes is cart-tested.
